result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.add_prism_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a prism graph to the current graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L3667-L3778){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_prism_graph( n, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Prism graph](/assets/graphs/add-prism-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three prism graphs side by side for n=3, 4, and 5, each drawn as an outer n-cycle around an inner n-cycle with n rungs joining matching nodes. That gives 2n nodes and 3n edges: 6 and 9, 8 and 12, 10 and 15." width="100%"} Creates two parallel n-cycles connected by n vertical edges, forming a 3D prism structure when visualized. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in each cycle (minimum `3`). [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional node type/category for all nodes. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, label nodes with their IDs. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional relationship label for all edges. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A prism graph joins two parallel `n`-cycles with `n` "rung" edges connecting corresponding nodes, so it always has `2n` nodes and `3n` edges (`n` edges per cycle, plus `n` rungs). Here `n=5` gives `10` nodes and `15` edges: ::: {#95f3979f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_prism_graph(5) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (10, 15) ``` ::: :::
